html:
The Anglo-Maratha Wars were three wars between the East India Company and the Maratha Confederacy between 1775 and 1818. The last one removed the only Indian power that could still match the British.

The first, from 1775 to 1782, began when the Company backed a rival claimant to the office of peshwa. It went badly: a British army surrendered at Wadgaon in 1779. The peace of 1782 left things as they were.

By 1800 the Maratha chiefs, the Peshwa, Scindia, Holkar, Bhonsle and Gaekwad, were fighting each other. In 1802 the Peshwa, driven from Pune by Holkar, signed a treaty that put him under British protection.

The second war, from 1803 to 1805, followed. Arthur Wellesley beat Scindia's French-trained army at Assaye in the Deccan, which he later called his hardest battle. In the north General Lake took Delhi and with it the blind Mughal emperor.

The third, in 1817 and 1818, finished it. The Peshwa attacked the British at Pune, was beaten and gave himself up. His office was abolished and he was pensioned off near Kanpur. The other chiefs kept reduced states under British control.

From 1818 the Company was the paramount power in India. Only Punjab and Sindh remained outside.
sum: The Anglo-Maratha Wars were three wars between the East India Company and the Maratha Confederacy between 1775 and 1818. The last one removed the only Indian power that could still match the British.
